document.title: Overdose Data to Action: 2024 Annual Surveillance Report of Preliminary Trends in Drug Overdoses in Dallas County

provenance_note: Every value below is an OBSERVED, PUBLISHED figure transcribed verbatim from the OD2A PDF with page/section/figure citation. No value is estimated, imputed, or extrapolated. Rankings without per-unit counts are recorded as rankings only. Chart labels that cannot be unambiguously attributed by series/year from the PDF text layout are stored as flagged raw token arrays, not attributed values. Counts < 10 are suppressed in the source and noted.

data_sources.mortality: Texas Department of State Health Services Vital Statistics. Data as of August 14, 2025.
data_sources.comparative_rates: CDC Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (WONDER). Data extracted April 2, 2025.
data_sources.emergency_department: Electronic Surveillance System for the Early Notification of Community-based Epidemics (ESSENCE). Data as of August 14, 2025.

facts.metric: Total overdose deaths, calendar year 2024 (provisional)
facts.printed: As of August 14, 2025, a total of 558 overdose deaths were reported in 2024 compared to 628 in 2023.

facts.metric: Total overdose deaths, calendar year 2023
facts.printed: As of August 14, 2025, a total of 558 overdose deaths were reported in 2024 compared to 628 in 2023.

facts.metric: Demographic groups with highest death burden
facts.printed: The highest burden of deaths occurred among males, White individuals, and adults aged 35-64 years.

facts.metric: Opioid-related ED visit change, Hispanic individuals, 2023-2024
facts.printed: visits increased by 2.8% among Hispanic individuals, while decreasing 10.5% among non-Hispanic Black individuals and 3% among non-Hispanic White individuals.

facts.metric: Opioid-related ED visit change, non-Hispanic Black, 2023-2024
facts.printed: decreasing 10.5% among non-Hispanic Black individuals

facts.metric: Opioid-related ED visit change, non-Hispanic White, 2023-2024
facts.printed: 3% among non-Hispanic White individuals

facts.metric: Dallas County population
facts.printed: Dallas County is the second-largest county in Texas with a population of 2.6 million people.

facts.metric: Households speaking a language other than English
facts.printed: 40% of Dallas County households speak a language other than English

facts.metric: Share of those households with limited-English proficiency
facts.printed: approximately 1 in 5 of those households have limited-English proficiency, the highest percentage in the region.

facts.metric: Change in confirmed drug overdose deaths, 2016-2024
facts.printed: Between 2016 and 2024, the number of confirmed drug overdose deaths in Dallas County increased by 77.1%.

facts.metric: All drug overdose deaths by year
facts.printed: Figure 1a. All Drug Overdose Deaths by Year in Dallas County, TX, 2016-2024 (values labeled on bars).
facts.note: Per-bar labels transcribed directly from Figure 1a. Sum = 4,028, which matches the total explicitly printed on p9.

facts.metric: Overdose crude mortality rate change, Dallas County, 2018-2024
facts.printed: Between 2018 and 2024, overdose crude mortality rates in Dallas County increased by 61%, from 12.9 to 20.8 per 100,000 individuals.

facts.metric: Overdose crude mortality rate change, Texas, 2018-2024
facts.printed: significantly outpacing the 49.5% increase seen in Texas

facts.metric: Overdose crude mortality rate change, United States, 2018-2024
facts.printed: and the 9.9% increase in the United States

facts.metric: Figure 1b crude mortality rate chart labels (raw, unattributed)
facts.note: Raw numeric labels scraped from Figure 1b (US / Texas / Dallas County lines). Per-series/per-year attribution is NOT unambiguous from the PDF layout and is therefore NOT asserted; only the text-stated Dallas 12.9->20.8 (2018->2024) values are attributed above.

facts.metric: Accidental overdose deaths change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: Accidental overdoses made up most deaths between 2016 and 2024, increasing by almost 90% during that period.

facts.metric: Suicide overdose deaths change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: deaths resulting from suicide saw a smaller increase of 4% during the same period.

facts.metric: Deaths from opioids alone change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: Deaths attributed solely to opioids (no other drug present) rose by 17%

facts.metric: Deaths from opioids + stimulants combined change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: the combination of opioids and stimulants saw a dramatic increase of 260%.

facts.metric: Deaths from stimulants alone change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: Deaths from stimulants alone climbed by 167%.

facts.metric: Fentanyl-related deaths change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: From 2016 to 2024, fentanyl deaths surged by an alarming 1,550%.

facts.metric: Methamphetamine-related deaths change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: methamphetamine-related deaths increased by 319%

facts.metric: Cocaine-related deaths change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: cocaine increased by 148%

facts.metric: Heroin-related deaths change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: There has been a decrease in deaths due to heroin by 69%

facts.metric: Treatment (prescription) opioid deaths change, 2016-2024
facts.printed: and treatment opioids by 31%

facts.metric: All drug overdose deaths by sex and year
facts.printed: Figure 4. All Drug Overdose Deaths by Sex (bar labels).
facts.note: Two-series bar labels transcribed from Figure 4; per-year female+male sums equal the Figure 1a annual totals, confirming the transcription.

facts.metric: All drug overdose deaths by ethnicity (Fig 5, raw tokens)
facts.printed: Figure 5. All Drug Overdose Deaths by Ethnicity (Black, Hispanic, Other, White), 2016-2024.
facts.note: Figure 5 is a stacked/grouped bar whose per-series-per-year labels cannot be unambiguously attributed from the PDF text layout; per the no-extrapolation rule, individual counts are NOT recorded. Qualitative finding: highest deaths among White population (see p6 narrative).

facts.metric: All drug overdose deaths by age group (Fig 6, raw)
facts.printed: Figure 6. All Drug Overdose Deaths by Age group, 2016-2024 (groups 0-17,18-24,25-34,35-44,45-54,55-64,65+).
facts.note: Stacked bar; per-series-per-year labels not unambiguously attributable from layout, so counts are not recorded. Narrative (p6): highest among individuals aged 35-64.

facts.metric: All drug overdose deaths by educational status (share of total)
facts.printed: overdose deaths were most prevalent among individuals who completed high school or had a GED (43.1%), followed by those who completed 9th-12th grade (17.8%).
facts.note: Percentages transcribed directly from labeled bars in Figure 7.

facts.metric: Marital status with highest overdose deaths (ranking)
facts.printed: the highest number of overdose deaths occurred among individuals who had never been married, followed by those who were divorced.
facts.note: Ranking only; Figure 8 prints no per-category counts.

facts.metric: Top residence ZIP codes by overdose deaths, 2016-2024 (ranking)
facts.printed: ZIP codes 75217, 75216, and 75215 recorded the highest number of drug overdose deaths between 2016 and 2024.
facts.note: Ranking only; Figure 9 map prints no per-ZIP counts.

facts.metric: Total overdose deaths, 2016-2024 window
facts.printed: approximately 60.9% of the total 4,028 overdose deaths in Dallas County occurred within the city of Dallas.
facts.note: Explicitly printed total; equals the sum of Figure 1a annual bar labels.

facts.metric: Share of overdose deaths within City of Dallas, 2016-2024
facts.printed: approximately 60.9% of the total 4,028 overdose deaths in Dallas County occurred within the city of Dallas, accounting for 2,455 fatalities.

facts.metric: Fentanyl-related death demographic findings

value.2016_2024_by_age_race: Hispanic aged 25-34 highest, then White aged 35-44

facts.printed: Between 2016 and 2024, fentanyl-related deaths were highest among White individuals, particularly males and those in the 25-34 age group. In 2024, however, Hispanic males had the highest number of fentanyl-related deaths across all combined sex and race/ethnicity categories.
facts.note: Figures 11a-c print grouped-bar labels not unambiguously attributable from layout; only the narrative findings recorded.

facts.metric: Cocaine-related death demographic findings

value.2024_highest_age_race: Black individuals aged 55-64, then Black individuals aged 65+
value.consistent: Black males highest, then Hispanic males, then Black females

facts.printed: Between 2016 and 2024, the highest number of cocaine-related deaths occurred among Black males, particularly those aged 55-64. ... Black males consistently accounted for the highest number of overdose deaths, followed by Hispanic males and Black females.
facts.note: Hispanic females suppressed (<10) in both years and not displayed. Figures 12a-c grouped-bar labels not unambiguously attributable; only narrative recorded.

facts.metric: Methamphetamine-related death demographic findings
facts.printed: Between 2023 and 2024, methamphetamine-related deaths declined overall, with the highest numbers observed among White individuals, males, and adults aged 55-64. However, deaths increased among Hispanic males over the same period.
facts.note: Figures 13a-c grouped-bar labels not unambiguously attributable; only narrative recorded.

facts.metric: All-drug overdose ED visits change, 2018-2024
facts.printed: The total number of all drug overdose-related EDVs increased by 51.4% between 2018 and 2024.

facts.metric: All-drug overdose ED visits change, 2023-2024
facts.printed: Between 2023 and 2024, it declined slightly by 5.2%.

facts.metric: All-drug overdose ED visits by year
facts.printed: Figure 14. All Drug Overdose EDVs by Year (bar labels).
facts.note: Bar labels transcribed from Figure 14; 3663/2419 = 1.514 confirms the printed +51.4% (2018-2024).
facts.section: Historical Trends of Drug Overdose Emergency Visits by Year

facts.metric: Opioid-related ED visits, 2024
facts.printed: In 2024, the total number of opioid-related emergency department visits was 793, reflecting a 5.7% decline compared to 2023.

facts.metric: Opioid-related ED visits by year
facts.printed: Figure 15a. Opioid-related Overdose EDVs by Year (bar labels 841, 793).

facts.metric: Opioid-related ED visits change, Q4 2024
facts.printed: opioid overdose-related EDVs showed fluctuations, ultimately declining by 7.1% in the fourth quarter of 2024.

facts.metric: Opioid-related ED visits by quarter (Fig 15b, raw tokens)
facts.note: Raw quarterly bar labels scraped from Figure 15b. Exact quarter-to-value mapping is not unambiguous from the layout, so no per-quarter attribution is asserted; only the text-stated Q4 2024 -7.1% is recorded above.

facts.metric: Opioid-related ED visit monthly peaks
facts.printed: peaks observed in March, May, and October of 2024, and in March, June, and September of 2023.
facts.note: Figure 16 monthly bar labels not unambiguously attributable; only the peak months are recorded.

facts.metric: Share of opioid ED visits among ages 18-44, 2024
facts.printed: In 2024, individuals aged 18-24, 25-34, and 35-44 collectively accounted for nearly 69.2% of all opioid overdose-related ED visits.

facts.metric: Male-to-female ratio of opioid ED visits, 2024
facts.printed: Males had nearly 2.1 times as many opioid overdose-related EDVs as females.

facts.metric: Top residence ZIPs by opioid ED visits, 2024 (ranking)
facts.printed: Geospatial analysis in 2024 showed the number of opioid-related emergency department visits was highest among residents of zip code 75235, followed by 75243, 75228, 75042, 75217, 75230.
facts.note: Ranking only; Figure 21 map prints no per-ZIP counts.

facts.metric: ZIPs with highest overdose fatality concentration (conclusion)
facts.printed: certain areas in Dallas County, notably ZIP codes 75217, 75216, and 75215, have been identified as having the highest concentrations of overdose fatalities.

facts.metric: Age groups bearing highest death burden (conclusion)
facts.printed: with males and specific age groups, including those aged 25-54 years, consistently bearing the highest overdose death burden.
